physiology.lthr_source: 30-min TT, April 2026 (race-validated at White River and Vermont)

exercises.name: Walking knee hugs
exercises.cue: Pull knee to chest, balance on standing leg for 1 second.

exercises.name: Walking quad pulls
exercises.cue: Tall posture, knee points down.

exercises.name: Leg swings — front/back
exercises.cue: Hold something for balance; relaxed, full range.

exercises.name: Leg swings — side/side
exercises.cue: Open the hip, don't twist the spine.

exercises.name: Walking lunges
exercises.cue: Front knee tracks over second toe; keep torso tall.

exercises.name: Glute bridges
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes at the top; ribs down.

exercises.name: High knees
exercises.cue: Quick turnover; emphasize lift, not speed.

exercises.name: Strides (quality days only)
exercises.cue: Build to ~85% of 5K pace over 20 sec. 60 sec full recovery between. Skip on easy days.

pre_run.notes: Do this BEFORE every run. Strides are for Friday aerobic runs and the Tuesday slot's warm-up only; skip them on recovery days, long runs and the AeT test. Recovery weeks 1-2: mobility items only, gently. HEEL: keep ankle mobility pain-free; no end-range dorsiflexion loading while the posterior heel is reactive.

exercises.name: Walking cooldown
exercises.cue: Walk until HR is below 110 bpm before stretching.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
exercises.cue: Tuck pelvis under to feel the stretch in the front of the hip too.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch (bent + straight knee)
exercises.cue: Two angles per side, knee straight (gastroc) and bent (soleus). Stretch on FLAT ground - do not hang the heel off a step while the posterior heel is reactive (compression at the attachment).

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Squeeze the back glute first, THEN lean forward.

exercises.name: Pigeon stretch
exercises.cue: Square hips. If knee complains, lie back instead (figure-4 supine).

exercises.name: Foam roll quads, IT band, calves (optional)
exercises.cue: 60 seconds per area; pause and breathe on tender spots.

post_run.notes: Within 15 min of finishing. Especially after long runs, B2B days and descent sessions. Walking cooldown to HR < 110 first.

exercises.name: Foot tripod + short-foot set
exercises.cue: Barefoot or socks. Set the arch before loading it.

exercises.name: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks
exercises.cue: Half-kneel, knee over toes, heel down - pain-free range only; stop short of any posterior-heel pinch.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.cue: 2 s squeeze at top.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
exercises.cue: Slow and full range; the knee-gate warmup — no loaded knee work until these feel silent.

exercises.name: Bodyweight step-down (low box)
exercises.cue: Final knee check before any loaded step work.

pre_lower.notes: KNEE GATE lives here: loaded step-downs/step-ups only after the bodyweight versions are pain-free and the knee is warm.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch (straight + bent knee)
exercises.cue: Both angles (gastroc and soleus) on FLAT ground - no heel hanging off a step while the heel is reactive.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Back glute on first, then lean.

exercises.name: Ankle dorsiflexion mobilization (wall)
exercises.cue: Knee to wall, heel down, pain-free range only.

post_lower.notes: NEW post-lower split (replaces the old single post_strength). Lower-body specific: calves/ankle/hip get the cooldown minutes.

exercises.name: Thoracic opener over foam roller
exercises.cue: Gentle extension. Deprioritized vs last cycle (pole-driven need is gone) but kept as a short reset.

post_upper.notes: NEW post-upper split — short shoulder/torso reset.

daily_routines.title: Foot & Arch Correctives (pronation program)

exercises.name: Short-foot activation
exercises.cue: Barefoot. Lift the arch without curling toes.

exercises.name: Toe yoga
exercises.cue: Big toe down, little toes up; then reverse.

exercises.name: Heel walks
exercises.cue: Toes up, walk on heels across the room.

exercises.name: Big-toe extension mobilization
exercises.cue: Kneel, toes tucked, gentle sit-back. Big-toe range for push-off.

exercises.name: Calf raise with eversion bias
exercises.cue: Rise with slight outward pressure — anti-pronation pattern.

daily_routines.notes: NON-NEGOTIABLE, every day of the cycle (right-foot pronation program). Pair with the daily collagen + vitamin C dose on non-lifting days.

daily_routines.title: Hip & Lateral-Chain Activation

exercises.name: Clamshells (band)
exercises.cue: Pelvis still; open from the hip.

exercises.name: Side-lying hip abduction
exercises.cue: Heel leads, toe slightly down — glute med, not TFL.

exercises.name: Banded lateral walk
exercises.cue: Athletic stance, steps controlled both directions.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance reach
exercises.cue: Stand on one leg, reach the free foot to 3 points of a clock.

daily_routines.notes: P1 component (d) daily floor: the lateral-stability chain (pronating right foot -> lateral ankle -> lateral knee) gets touched every morning; the loaded version lives in Lower B.

daily_routines.title: Shoulder & Scapular Maintenance

exercises.name: Band pull-aparts
exercises.cue: Squeeze shoulder blades; no shrug.

exercises.name: Band external rotation
exercises.cue: Elbow pinned to ribs. Left shoulder priority.

exercises.name: Scapular wall slides
exercises.cue: Forearms on wall, slide up without ribs flaring.

daily_routines.notes: Left-shoulder maintenance; matters more from January with ~37 mi of race poling ahead.

daily_routines.title: Evening Heel & Tendon Isometrics (FR-x)

exercises.name: Bent-knee soleus isometric (wall lean or loaded seated)
exercises.cue: ~70% effort, heel on the floor. The posterior-heel dose: frequency beats volume.

exercises.name: Resisted eversion isometric (band)
exercises.cue: Both sides; right +1 set.

phase_overrides.modification: Holds 30-45 s at moderate effort; mild heel discomfort (<= 2/10) that eases during the hold is fine - isometrics are analgesic.

daily_routines.notes: REPLACES tendon_isometrics_evening (Vermont cycle) with the posterior heel as the priority site. Skip on Lower A/B days (the session covers it). Run coach's read on the heel: steep-ascent load -> more calf isometrics + graded practice at those grades. Not a diagnosis: a clinician look if it persists > 2 weeks or returns in training.

daily_routines.title: Daily Mobility (8 min)

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Glute on first, then lean.

exercises.name: Open-book thoracic rotation
exercises.cue: Pole and vest posture.

daily_routines.notes: Range the long hours and the poles take away. Any time of day; pairs well with the evening isometrics.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.notes: Autumn blood work suggested (25-OH vitamin D, ferritin, CBC) before the winter volume block - dose by result. Do not supplement iron without a low ferritin result.

supplements.name: Omega-3 fish oil (EPA/DHA)
supplements.rationale: Anti-inflammatory support without blunting adaptation (unlike NSAIDs, which stay OFF around loading).

supplements.name: Collagen peptides + Vitamin C
supplements.timing: 30-60 min BEFORE lower/tendon strength sessions; on non-lifting days, with the morning foot-corrective block
supplements.rationale: Peri-loading collagen availability for tendon remodeling — the P1 nutritional lever. Daily low-dose beats one big weekly dose because collagen synthesis has a refractory window.
supplements.notes: THE priority supplement this block. Never skipped on Lower A / Lower B days.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.timing: post-run or post-strength, any consistent daily slot
supplements.rationale: Strength/power support during the HSR block; consistency matters more than timing.

supplements.name: Whey protein isolate
supplements.timing: post-session windows and to top up daily protein
supplements.rationale: Hits the 1.7-1.9 g/kg/day protein target that tissue remodeling at 50 demands.

supplements.name: Magnesium glycinate
supplements.rationale: Sleep quality — recovery is the P1 multiplier.

supplements.name: Electrolytes (SaltStick)
supplements.dose: Temperature-tiered: < 12 C none scheduled (gel + mix cover it); 12-22 C 1 capsule/60 min; > 22 C 1 capsule/40-45 min
supplements.rationale: Vermont sodium (515-675 mg/hr) was deliberately low for 56 F and caused no cramping; Tuscany's 0-30 C swing needs a tiered rate, not a flat one.

supplements.name: Caffeine (GU Roctane caffeine gels)
supplements.dose: 35 mg per caffeinated gel. Training runs > 3 h: 1-3 in the final third. Evening/dark sessions: one at dusk (test). Race: see the 4/17 override (<= ~400 mg total).
supplements.timing: Final third of long efforts; dusk on headlamp runs
supplements.rationale: Vermont: 3 caffeinated gels in the last 2.5 h, clean. Tuscany adds a 15-17 h day and a dark finish - timing is tested on 1/10, 1/30, 3/7, 3/21.

sessions.notes: Post-Vermont re-entry. No HSR, no eccentric overload yet. Pain <= 2/10 during and back to baseline next morning = load is right. Progress LOAD, not reps. Collagen 15 g + vitamin C 250 mg 30-60 min before (nutrition plan).

sessions.title: AeT HEART-RATE DRIFT TEST #1 (treadmill, 3%)
sessions.key_cue: Uphill Athlete protocol. SETUP: treadmill at 3% (same machine and grade every test), CHEST STRAP (wet the contacts), fan on, cool room, same time of day and same pre-test meal as test #1, no caffeine in the 3 h before, after a rest day. WARM-UP 15 min: walk, then build speed until HR sits stable for 2-3 min at the STARTING HR. STARTING HR: test #1 = 145 bpm (between your race-validated ~136-150 band and the 149 working cap). Retests start at the last measured AeT. LAP. TEST 60 min at ONE locked speed and grade - do not touch the controls. LAP at 30:00 and at 60:00. COOL-DOWN 10 min easy. RESULT = avg HR 2nd half / avg HR 1st half - 1. <3.5% = your AeT is higher: retest +5 bpm. 3.5-5.0% = AeT = your starting HR. >5% = started above AeT: retest -5 bpm. GATE: AeT >= 152 (within 10% of LTHR 168) -> no aerobic deficiency; Z3 sessions switch on. Below 152 -> Z1-2 only, retest in 4-6 weeks. FIT to the Drive inbox the same day.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Test. The hr_cap_bpm here is only the provisional alert; the starting HR in the cue governs. Treadmill incline is NOT counted in elevation_gain_ft (no matching descent, no eccentric load). The result re-anchors EVERY AeT-referenced cap in this plan by patch revision (hr_anchor field). THE GATE for the whole cycle: it decides whether and when Z3 enters the plan, and it resets every easy-day ceiling. If the result is inconclusive (<3.5% or >5%), the retest takes Tuesday 10/20's slot.

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 2 x 8 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.
sessions.fueling_notes: 1 gel at 45 min if over 75 min.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Aerobic quality (priority 1 - uphill running at low HR). Lower A this evening. SURFACE: gravel/dirt road, smooth trail or a treadmill at the named grade - the band is the point, the surface is not (terrain_intent grade; Terrain_Substitution_Rules_v1). CONDITIONAL: if test #1 on 10/13 was inconclusive, this slot becomes AeT retest #1b at the adjusted starting HR (+/-5 bpm), same protocol; the climbing session is dropped for the week.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: TI FOUNDATION DRILLS: balance/superman glide, skate position, then zipper and switch drills in 25 m repeats with full rest. Stop each drill before form breaks. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

sessions.title: Easy TI swim

BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + SHORT WHOLE STROKE: ~10 min drills, then 25-50 m whole-stroke repeats. Focus: head-spine alignment, patient lead hand, 2-beat kick. Count strokes per length (SPL) and keep it steady. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

daily_targets.notes: FUELING LADDER (FR-w: the problem is calorie MIX, not volume). BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). PEAK W23-26: race protocol v1 (overrides 3/7, 3/21). One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline.

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 3 x 10 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. HILL SPRINTS x6: 8-10 s max-effort uphill at +8..+12% (steeper only after 4 clean weeks), full walk-down recovery 2-3 min. Alactic - HR is irrelevant, so these are NOT gated by the AeT test (Uphill Athlete permits them in an aerobic-deficiency base). GATED ON: the single-leg hop test (strength plan W6) AND a quiet posterior heel. First thing pulled on any heel, Achilles or forefoot signal. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: AeT HEART-RATE DRIFT TEST #2 (treadmill, 3%)
sessions.key_cue: Uphill Athlete protocol. SETUP: treadmill at 3% (same machine and grade every test), CHEST STRAP (wet the contacts), fan on, cool room, same time of day and same pre-test meal as test #1, no caffeine in the 3 h before, after a rest day. WARM-UP 15 min: walk, then build speed until HR sits stable for 2-3 min at the STARTING HR. STARTING HR: test #1 = 145 bpm (between your race-validated ~136-150 band and the 149 working cap). Retests start at the last measured AeT. LAP. TEST 60 min at ONE locked speed and grade - do not touch the controls. LAP at 30:00 and at 60:00. COOL-DOWN 10 min easy. RESULT = avg HR 2nd half / avg HR 1st half - 1. <3.5% = your AeT is higher: retest +5 bpm. 3.5-5.0% = AeT = your starting HR. >5% = started above AeT: retest -5 bpm. GATE: AeT >= 152 (within 10% of LTHR 168) -> no aerobic deficiency; Z3 sessions switch on. Below 152 -> Z1-2 only, retest in 4-6 weeks. FIT to the Drive inbox the same day.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Test. The hr_cap_bpm here is only the provisional alert; the starting HR in the cue governs. Treadmill incline is NOT counted in elevation_gain_ft (no matching descent, no eccentric load). The result re-anchors EVERY AeT-referenced cap in this plan by patch revision (hr_anchor field). Retest #2, 6 weeks after #1. Start at the AeT measured on 10/13.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + SHORT WHOLE STROKE: ~10 min drills, then 25-50 m whole-stroke repeats. Focus: head-spine alignment, patient lead hand, 2-beat kick. Count strokes per length (SPL) and keep it steady. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

sessions.title: Easy TI swim - active recovery

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 2 x 10 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. HILL SPRINTS x6: 8-10 s max-effort uphill at +8..+12% (steeper only after 4 clean weeks), full walk-down recovery 2-3 min. Alactic - HR is irrelevant, so these are NOT gated by the AeT test (Uphill Athlete permits them in an aerobic-deficiency base). GATED ON: the single-leg hop test (strength plan W6) AND a quiet posterior heel. First thing pulled on any heel, Achilles or forefoot signal. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: GATE D #1 - December qualifying run
sessions.key_cue: GATE D QUALIFYING RUN (criteria agreed August, unchanged): 20-22 mi ROLLING, RUNNABLE, with 3,000+ ft of DESCENT; the downs RUN, not hiked; then a clean 48-hour symptom window. POLE-FREE for comparability (ask #6). Route: Hutchinson loop x2.5 or an equivalent rolling non-technical loop that delivers >= 3,000 ft of descent - check the route's descent before you start. This is a tissue-tolerance test, NOT a race simulation: do not inflate it (cover note). HR capped at AeT on climbs; descents audited. SHOES: the Peregrine for BOTH gate runs - a shoe change between them would break comparability. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

sessions.title: GATE D #2 - December qualifying run
sessions.key_cue: GATE D QUALIFYING RUN (criteria agreed August, unchanged): 20-22 mi ROLLING, RUNNABLE, with 3,000+ ft of DESCENT; the downs RUN, not hiked; then a clean 48-hour symptom window. POLE-FREE for comparability (ask #6). Route: Hutchinson loop x2.5 or an equivalent rolling non-technical loop that delivers >= 3,000 ft of descent - check the route's descent before you start. This is a tissue-tolerance test, NOT a race simulation: do not inflate it (cover note). HR capped at AeT on climbs; descents audited. SHOES: the Peregrine for BOTH gate runs - a shoe change between them would break comparability. REPEAT: same route as #1 if at all possible, so the two are comparable. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.
sessions.fueling_notes: See nutrition day type long_run, or the date override where one exists.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Aerobic volume. LOAD-PATTERN GUARD: rolling non-technical terrain; never a cluster of long technical-descent runs (June 2026 lesson). Min 6 days between long runs. Intensity: GATE. FIT + 48-h symptom notes (heel, lateral ankle, knees, forefoot: morning ratings 0-10 on days +1 and +2) to Race Strategy; RS rules within a few days. PASS twice within three weeks -> the 103K is on. FAIL -> fallback is the 53K at the same event or a spring 50-miler, and this plan re-scopes by revision.

BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). sessions.title: Easy TI swim - active recovery
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 3 x 15 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. HILL SPRINTS x8: 8-10 s max-effort uphill at +8..+12% (steeper only after 4 clean weeks), full walk-down recovery 2-3 min. Alactic - HR is irrelevant, so these are NOT gated by the AeT test (Uphill Athlete permits them in an aerobic-deficiency base). GATED ON: the single-leg hop test (strength plan W6) AND a quiet posterior heel. First thing pulled on any heel, Achilles or forefoot signal. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.
sessions.fueling_notes: 1 gel at 45 min if over 75 min.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Aerobic quality (priority 1 - uphill running at low HR). Lower A this evening. SURFACE: gravel/dirt road, smooth trail or a treadmill at the named grade - the band is the point, the surface is not (terrain_intent grade; Terrain_Substitution_Rules_v1).

sessions.title: AeT HEART-RATE DRIFT TEST #3 (treadmill, 3%)
sessions.key_cue: Uphill Athlete protocol. SETUP: treadmill at 3% (same machine and grade every test), CHEST STRAP (wet the contacts), fan on, cool room, same time of day and same pre-test meal as test #1, no caffeine in the 3 h before, after a rest day. WARM-UP 15 min: walk, then build speed until HR sits stable for 2-3 min at the STARTING HR. STARTING HR: test #1 = 145 bpm (between your race-validated ~136-150 band and the 149 working cap). Retests start at the last measured AeT. LAP. TEST 60 min at ONE locked speed and grade - do not touch the controls. LAP at 30:00 and at 60:00. COOL-DOWN 10 min easy. RESULT = avg HR 2nd half / avg HR 1st half - 1. <3.5% = your AeT is higher: retest +5 bpm. 3.5-5.0% = AeT = your starting HR. >5% = started above AeT: retest -5 bpm. GATE: AeT >= 152 (within 10% of LTHR 168) -> no aerobic deficiency; Z3 sessions switch on. Below 152 -> Z1-2 only, retest in 4-6 weeks. FIT to the Drive inbox the same day.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Test. The hr_cap_bpm here is only the provisional alert; the starting HR in the cue governs. Treadmill incline is NOT counted in elevation_gain_ft (no matching descent, no eccentric load). The result re-anchors EVERY AeT-referenced cap in this plan by patch revision (hr_anchor field). Retest #3 - sets zones for the Oracle block.

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 3 x 15 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. HILL SPRINTS x8: 8-10 s max-effort uphill at +8..+12% (steeper only after 4 clean weeks), full walk-down recovery 2-3 min. Alactic - HR is irrelevant, so these are NOT gated by the AeT test (Uphill Athlete permits them in an aerobic-deficiency base). GATED ON: the single-leg hop test (strength plan W6) AND a quiet posterior heel. First thing pulled on any heel, Achilles or forefoot signal. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 4 x 15 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

daily_targets.notes: FUELING LADDER (FR-w: the problem is calorie MIX, not volume). BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). BUILD W14-22: 250-280 cal/hr as a MIX - gels ~50%, half-strength drink ~25%, real food ~25% every 45-60 min - so no single source runs over ~150 cal/hr (Vermont's fullness came at ~365 cal/hr, mostly gel + drink). PEAK W23-26: race protocol v1 (overrides 3/7, 3/21). One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline.

A TRAINING RACE, HR-led: capped at AeT all day; in the final 10 mi only, by feel up to AeT+5 if everything is clean (a declared, alerted allowance - the Vermont sting lesson). JOBS: J-1 first exposure past 31 mi (hours 7-11); J-2 real food + aid-station fueling on an ~11 h day; pacing discipline when tired. SHOE GATE G1 (RS FR-aa): run it in the CANDIDATE shoe - proves stability and toe protection on rocky singletrack (not hard-surface durability; that is G2 on 3/7). POLES: start without, pick them up at an early aid - a mechanics rehearsal of the Gallina pickup and the quiver stow (short-pitch course). AID ROUTINE: the fixed, no-social-dwell routine (ask #7). NOT a descent test. || FALLBACK (if you don't travel): the same Saturday, one supported CONTINUOUS 8-10 h day on local rolling trail/road, ~34-38 mi / ~4,500 ft, starting 05:30 so the first ~1.5 h is by headlamp (sunrise ~07:05); support = car/cache loop every 2-2.5 h run as 'aid stations'; same jobs, same fueling protocol, same HR rule. sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 2 x 12 min of continuous climbing at +3..+7%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.

sessions.title: AeT HEART-RATE DRIFT TEST #4 (treadmill, 3%)
sessions.key_cue: Uphill Athlete protocol. SETUP: treadmill at 3% (same machine and grade every test), CHEST STRAP (wet the contacts), fan on, cool room, same time of day and same pre-test meal as test #1, no caffeine in the 3 h before, after a rest day. WARM-UP 15 min: walk, then build speed until HR sits stable for 2-3 min at the STARTING HR. STARTING HR: test #1 = 145 bpm (between your race-validated ~136-150 band and the 149 working cap). Retests start at the last measured AeT. LAP. TEST 60 min at ONE locked speed and grade - do not touch the controls. LAP at 30:00 and at 60:00. COOL-DOWN 10 min easy. RESULT = avg HR 2nd half / avg HR 1st half - 1. <3.5% = your AeT is higher: retest +5 bpm. 3.5-5.0% = AeT = your starting HR. >5% = started above AeT: retest -5 bpm. GATE: AeT >= 152 (within 10% of LTHR 168) -> no aerobic deficiency; Z3 sessions switch on. Below 152 -> Z1-2 only, retest in 4-6 weeks. FIT to the Drive inbox the same day.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Test. The hr_cap_bpm here is only the provisional alert; the starting HR in the cue governs. Treadmill incline is NOT counted in elevation_gain_ft (no matching descent, no eccentric load). The result re-anchors EVERY AeT-referenced cap in this plan by patch revision (hr_anchor field). Retest #4, post-Oracle - zones for the Tuscany-specific block.

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 2 x 20 min of continuous climbing at +4..+8%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. HILL SPRINTS x6: 8-10 s max-effort uphill at +8..+12% (steeper only after 4 clean weeks), full walk-down recovery 2-3 min. Alactic - HR is irrelevant, so these are NOT gated by the AeT test (Uphill Athlete permits them in an aerobic-deficiency base). GATED ON: the single-leg hop test (strength plan W6) AND a quiet posterior heel. First thing pulled on any heel, Achilles or forefoot signal. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. sessions.title: Long run - HEADLAMP #3 (05:00 race-start sim)
sessions.key_cue: RACE-START SIMULATION: start 05:00 (sunrise ~06:45) with the race breakfast at ~03:00 (nutrition override). First ~1.75 h by headlamp including a descent, pole-free; PICK UP POLES at ~mi 8 (the Gallina switch rehearsal) and use them for the rest. SURFACE (RS memo 3c): hilly dirt / fire / carriage road - Rockefeller Preserve or Minnewaska carriage roads, Harriman woods roads. Tuscany's front 2/3 is hard gravel farm road; this is the most specific volume surface available. RACE WEIGHT: carry the Tuscany mandatory kit - 1 L water minimum, waterproof jacket, thermal blanket, whistle, phone, headlamp + spare, cup (cover-note ask #2). POLES (Black Diamond Carbon Z): deploy on sustained climbs >= +8% and on steep descents <= -10%; stowed in the quiver elsewhere. HEADLAMP SESSION (ask #1): carry the race headlamp + spare; the dark section includes a descent - cadence up, stride short, eyes 3-4 m ahead. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Aerobic climbing - run the climbs at or below AeT
sessions.key_cue: After a 15-min Z1-2 warm-up: 3 x 20 min (or one 50-min block on the treadmill at 6-7%) of continuous climbing at +4..+8%, jog/walk down between. Remainder of the run Z1-2 on rolling terrain. RULE: HR at the alert (AeT) -> hike immediately until AeT-5, then run again. Hiking to stay aerobic is the session working, not failing. READ-OUT (FR tracking ask #4): lap-press every climb block; RS reports run_pct and mean HR on +5..+10% versus the Vermont baseline (debrief s3: ~60% run share on +5..+10% late). Target over the cycle: crossover up from ~7-8% at unchanged HR. WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Long run
sessions.key_cue: Hilly loop with the longest sustained climbs available (Perkins Memorial / Bear Mountain area). Poles from the first climb >= +8%. SURFACE (RS memo 3c): hilly dirt / fire / carriage road - Rockefeller Preserve or Minnewaska carriage roads, Harriman woods roads. Tuscany's front 2/3 is hard gravel farm road; this is the most specific volume surface available. WET-FEET TEST (RS memo 3d): take an ankle-deep creek crossing in the first hour (walk it - Tuscany rule), then run on in wet socks - the sock/lube/shoe system is the test. Skip if the water is icy. LATE ROUGH-DESCENT BLOCK (ban amendment, athlete 9/30): in the LAST HOUR, 1.5 mi at -8..-15% on RUTTED/ROCKY FIRE ROAD - never sustained technical singletrack. POLES on, cadence 175+, short strides, quiet feet; toe protection is part of the test (Tuscany finishers lost toes at ~km 87). GATED: only if Gate D PASSED and the heel/ankle/knee gates are clean this week; otherwise run the block on a smooth non-technical descent. FIT flagged for RS (descent durability model). RACE WEIGHT: carry the Tuscany mandatory kit - 1 L water minimum, waterproof jacket, thermal blanket, whistle, phone, headlamp + spare, cup (cover-note ask #2). POLES (Black Diamond Carbon Z): deploy on sustained climbs >= +8% and on steep descents <= -10%; stowed in the quiver elsewhere. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Long run
sessions.key_cue: LAST BIG RUN - dress rehearsal: race kit, race breakfast, race fueling protocol v1 (override 3/21), poles, aid routine. Finish the final descent by headlamp if the timing allows (sunset ~19:15). SURFACE (RS memo 3c): hilly dirt / fire / carriage road - Rockefeller Preserve or Minnewaska carriage roads, Harriman woods roads. Tuscany's front 2/3 is hard gravel farm road; this is the most specific volume surface available. WET-FEET TEST (RS memo 3d): take an ankle-deep creek crossing in the first hour (walk it - Tuscany rule), then run on in wet socks - the sock/lube/shoe system is the test. Skip if the water is icy. LATE ROUGH-DESCENT BLOCK (ban amendment, athlete 9/30): in the LAST HOUR, 2.5-3 mi at -8..-15% on RUTTED/ROCKY FIRE ROAD - never sustained technical singletrack. POLES on, cadence 175+, short strides, quiet feet; toe protection is part of the test (Tuscany finishers lost toes at ~km 87). GATED: only if Gate D PASSED and the heel/ankle/knee gates are clean this week; otherwise run the block on a smooth non-technical descent. FIT flagged for RS (descent durability model). RACE WEIGHT: carry the Tuscany mandatory kit - 1 L water minimum, waterproof jacket, thermal blanket, whistle, phone, headlamp + spare, cup (cover-note ask #2). POLES (Black Diamond Carbon Z): deploy on sustained climbs >= +8% and on steep descents <= -10%; stowed in the quiver elsewhere. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

sessions.title: Long run
sessions.key_cue: Last 3-h+ run. Easy, poles, race kit. SURFACE (RS memo 3c): hilly dirt / fire / carriage road - Rockefeller Preserve or Minnewaska carriage roads, Harriman woods roads. Tuscany's front 2/3 is hard gravel farm road; this is the most specific volume surface available. LATE ROUGH-DESCENT BLOCK (ban amendment, athlete 9/30): in the LAST HOUR, 1 mi at -8..-15% on RUTTED/ROCKY FIRE ROAD - never sustained technical singletrack. POLES on, cadence 175+, short strides, quiet feet; toe protection is part of the test (Tuscany finishers lost toes at ~km 87). GATED: only if Gate D PASSED and the heel/ankle/knee gates are clean this week; otherwise run the block on a smooth non-technical descent. FIT flagged for RS (descent durability model). RACE WEIGHT: carry the Tuscany mandatory kit - 1 L water minimum, waterproof jacket, thermal blanket, whistle, phone, headlamp + spare, cup (cover-note ask #2). POLES (Black Diamond Carbon Z): deploy on sustained climbs >= +8% and on steep descents <= -10%; stowed in the quiver elsewhere. HR: capped at AeT on climbs (hike to stay under); descents audited. AID ROUTINE: loop past the car/cache and rehearse a fixed <= 2-min stop (bottles, food, out) - no social dwell (ask #7). WATCH ALERT: set a high-HR alert at the hr_cap_bpm value (FR-y) - it is a number the watch enforces, not one you remember.

daily_targets.notes: FUELING LADDER (FR-w: the problem is calorie MIX, not volume). BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). PEAK W23-26: race protocol v1 (overrides 3/7, 3/21). One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline.

sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). sessions.title: Easy TI swim
sessions.key_cue: DRILLS + CONTINUOUS EASY SWIMMING: ~10 min drills, then 200-400 m continuous at an easy, even SPL; bilateral breathing. EFFORT 3-4/10 throughout; if breathing gets ragged, go back to drills. HR is NOT capped: swim HR runs well below running HR at the same effort, so the running AeT cap does not apply - go by feel. SHOULDER RULE: stop at the first pinch at the front or top of the shoulder (left is the priority side); no paddles; hands enter wide ('railroad tracks'), never crossing the midline. KICK: relaxed 2-beat; ease it off if the calf or posterior heel tightens; no breaststroke kick (knees). Gentle wall push-offs.
sessions.notes: Cross-training (athlete, rev 2.2): general aerobic + upper-body work, light on the legs. NOT counted in run mileage, vertical or the ramp guard; counted in weekly hours. If the left shoulder reacts, swimming is dropped BEFORE Upper A (Upper A's cuff work is the protective part). Swim first, Upper B later (Upper B is push, so it complements the swim's pull).
